question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` continue accepting numerically equivalent `+`-prefixed and zero-padded decimal spellings, or should the Policy CLI intentionally require canonical decimal text?
rationale: Current code deliberately accepts these spellings, they produce the same cadence, and neither the existing error text nor the supplied docs establish a canonical-text requirement; changing that compatibility contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Preserve equivalent decimals
options.body: Keep accepting `+500` and zero-padded decimal spellings because they map to the same safe interval and are already supported.

options.title: Require canonical decimal text
options.body: Approve the compatibility break, document the canonical-only grammar, and require real CLI upgrade-oriented proof before merge.

options.title: Close the hardening proposal
options.body: Close this PR if canonical textual representation has no concrete user or safety benefit for the Policy watch interval.

recommendation.title: Preserve equivalent decimals
recommendation.body: Keep accepting `+500` and zero-padded decimal spellings because they map to the same safe interval and are already supported.

likelyOwner.reason: The available routing evidence most directly connects this person to recent Policy conformance and the affected command surface.
